pr_title: Prevent the quake window's borders from hanging onto adjacent monitors
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

We were making the quake window exactly the width of the monitor it was on, but that didn't account for the 1px of border on either side.		

## References
* megathread: #8888

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #10201
* [x] I work here
* [ ] Tests added/passed
* [n/a] Requires documentation to be updated

## Validation Steps Performed

It happened before, it doesn't anymore.

issue_context.title: 1px window border of the quake dropdown terminal "leaks" onto horizontally adjacent monitor:
issue_context.body:
I noticed a super minor thing when trying this out today: the 1px window border of the quake dropdown terminal "leaks" onto my horizontally adjacent monitor:

<details>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25607767/119579510-d0d52e80-bdbe-11eb-83e6-912161db2f2b.png)

</details>

Obviously this is hard to show on a screenshot, but IRL because of the bezel separating my screens I can clearly see the 1px gray border on the leftmost pixel row of my right monitor.

_Originally posted by @jantari in https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/8888#issuecomment-848329444_

review_comments: I really don't understand what this code is doing here. I'll approve it because it quite obviously can't break anything, but I fail to understand why we need to subtract half of ncSize. ncSize is the desktop size, minus the size of the window right? So why isn't this just set to `nearestMonitorInfo.rcWork.left` directly?
ncSize is the size of the Window's invisible 8-pixel borders :smile: (except it's not always 8, and it isn't uniform)
so we want to adjust based on the size of the invisible portion of the window border
